name: Black Hole in Thermal Equilibrium with Radiation
description: A static black hole in thermal equilibrium with a conformal scalar field, including its first order gravitational back reaction.
convention: In units $G=c=1$, the mass function is $m(r)=M(1+\epsilon\mu)$ and the redshift potential is $\rho-B$. The metric and its derived tensors are retained through first order in $\epsilon=\hbar/M^2$. The wall is at $R=r_{\rm B}$; the vacuum exterior has mass $m(R)$.
history: Radiation surrounds a black hole in thermal equilibrium, and its energy changes the surrounding geometry [york1993dressed, york1985equilibrium]. Don N. Page found an approximation for the stress of a conformal scalar field in the Hartle-Hawking state in 1982 [taylor2021backreaction, page1982thermal]. The state describes a black hole in equilibrium with thermal radiation [york1993dressed, page1982thermal]. K. W. Howard and Philip Candelas calculated the scalar field stress in 1984 and found it agreed qualitatively with the Page approximation [hochberg1994potential, howard1984stress].¶James W. York, Jr. calculated the gravitational effect of that radiation in 1985 for a free, massless scalar field coupled conformally to curvature [hochberg1994potential, york1985equilibrium]. He found the change to first order in Planck's constant $\hbar$ [hochberg1994potential, york1985equilibrium]. Static observers measure negative scalar field energy density near the horizon in the Page approximation [taylor2021backreaction, hochberg1994potential]. The radiation contribution to the mass is negative near the horizon and positive farther out [hochberg1994potential, hochberg1995canonical]. Its fractional contribution scales with $\hbar/(3840\pi M^2)$ ($M$ is the mass of the hole, $G=c=1$) [hochberg1994potential, hochberg1995canonical].¶A reflecting spherical wall encloses the hole and its radiation [hochberg1994potential, york1985equilibrium]. The interior joins a Schwarzschild exterior at the wall, with the mass outside accounting for the enclosed radiation [hochberg1994potential]. The field extends to infinity in the Page approximation, and a wall close to the horizon changes its modes [york1993dressed, hochberg1994potential]. A characteristic scalar wavelength is about $42M$, and York considered walls farther away when using this stress [york1993dressed].¶York studied a cavity held at fixed wall temperature in 1986 [hochberg1995canonical, york1986canonical]. The locally stable branch of the classical Schwarzschild problem has wall radius $r_{\rm B}$ between the horizon and the photon sphere ($2M<r_{\rm B}<3M$) [andre2021canonical, york1986canonical]. The two branches meet when the wall reaches the photon sphere ($r_{\rm B}=3M$) [andre2021canonical]. The horizon radius and Hawking temperature change when the quantum fields gravitate, and Carlos O. Loustó and Norma Graciela Sánchez calculated these changes for static spherical holes in 1988 and 1989 [lousto1988backreaction, lousto1989backreaction]. Chao-Guang Huang, Liao Liu, and Feng Xu added a thermodynamic surface near the horizon in 1991 [huang1991backreaction]. The energy and entropy of that surface contribute to the first law and reproduce the form of the quantum corrections calculated by York [huang1991backreaction].¶The spin of the field changes the gravitational force near the hole. David Hochberg and Thomas W. Kephart found a repulsive contribution from gauge fields in 1993 [hochberg1993gauge]. The entropy of the radiation also depends on its gravitational effect. Hochberg, Kephart, and York found a positive entropy correction for conformal scalar and gauge fields in 1993 with the energy at the wall held fixed [hochberg1993entropy]. That correction vanishes at the horizon and increases with radius at fixed black hole mass [hochberg1993entropy, york1993dressed]. Positivity of the entropy constrains the thermal stress tensor, as Oleg B. Zaslavskii derived that year [zaslavskii1993entropy].¶A black hole attached to a cosmic string can also equilibrate with Hawking radiation; C. F. P. Lee calculated the perturbed geometry and its thermodynamic stability in 1993 [lee1993radiation]. The event horizon acts as a two dimensional thermodynamic membrane in the model that Huang, Liu, and Zheng Zhao constructed that year [huang1993thermodynamical]. They described the hole and its curved space thermal radiation by a thermodynamic system in flat space [huang1993thermodynamical].¶The radiation changes the motion of test particles as well as the temperature of the hole. Hochberg, Kephart, and York calculated the effective potentials for null and timelike motion in 1994, including changes to particle capture and a dependence on the spin and number of quantum fields [hochberg1994potential]. Paul R. Anderson, William A. Hiscock, Janet Whitesell, and York calculated in 1994 how the coupling between the scalar field and curvature changes the geometry, obtaining the first order metric corrections for arbitrary curvature coupling with the energy fixed at a spherical wall [anderson1994nonconformal].¶The free energy determines which equilibrium configuration is favored at fixed wall temperature. Hochberg calculated the energy, entropy, and free energy of the semiclassical system in that canonical ensemble in 1995 [hochberg1995canonical]. The entropy corrections from conformal scalar and gauge fields can be negative near the horizon in this ensemble; the total entropy remains positive [hochberg1995canonical].¶Zaslavskii derived the one loop entropy of equilibrium radiation in 1996 directly from properties of the Hartle-Hawking state [zaslavskii1996entropy]. Zaslavskii also calculated how a reflecting shell contributes to the quantum temperature correction through the trace of the total stress tensor [zaslavskii1996boundary]. Hochberg and Sergey V. Sushkov calculated the metric perturbation from a conformal spin-2 field in 1996 with an approximate stress tensor [hochberg1996spin2]. They bounded the energy density of the field at the horizon by requiring positive entropy and small metric perturbations [hochberg1996spin2]. The scalar stress near the horizon differs from the Page approximation [matyjasek1998backreaction]. Jerzy Matyjasek used an improved analytic approximation in 1998 to recalculate the metric, temperature, entropy, and circular orbit potentials [matyjasek1998backreaction].¶Bei-Lok Hu, Alpan Raval, and Sukanya Sinha formulated a program for fluctuations and backreaction in 1999 using correlations of the thermal stress tensor [hu1999notes]. Antonio Campos and Hu derived an equation for stochastic metric perturbations and a relation between thermal fluctuations and dissipation that year in the weak gravitational field far from the hole [campos1999fluctuations]. Zaslavskii calculated the entropy contribution from massive field vacuum polarization in 2001, for field masses large compared with the Hawking temperature [zaslavskii2001entropy]. The vector field contribution is negative in this approximation; the total black hole entropy remains positive [zaslavskii2001entropy].¶Sinha, Raval, and Hu formulated the corresponding Einstein-Langevin equation for radial perturbations of a Schwarzschild hole in 2003 [sinha2003fluctuations]. The scalar field is in the Hartle-Hawking state, and the equation includes a fluctuating stress source and nonlocal dissipation [sinha2003fluctuations]. Nicholas G. Phillips and Hu calculated stress correlations in the optical Schwarzschild geometry that year and found that the Gaussian approximation loses accuracy at the fourth derivatives needed for stress fluctuations [phillips2003noise]. Zaslavskii included vacuum polarization outside a reflecting cavity in the temperature correction in 2003 [zaslavskii2003cavity]. The fields are in the Hartle-Hawking state inside the wall and the Boulware state outside; the exterior contribution can dominate the correction for a wall close to the horizon within the perturbative regime [zaslavskii2003cavity].¶Matyjasek recovered the Schwarzschild entropy corrections in 2006 from the horizon Noether charge of the massive field effective action in the infinite cavity limit [matyjasek2006entropy]. Matyjasek and Dariusz Tryniecki calculated in 2009 how a massive scalar field changes the geometry, including the next to leading term in the inverse mass expansion of the stress tensor [matyjasek2009backreaction]. They obtained corrections to the horizon and Hawking temperature for a Compton wavelength short compared with the curvature scale [matyjasek2009backreaction].¶Ardeshir Eftekharzadeh and coauthors calculated the scalar stress correlation in Schwarzschild spacetime at separated points in 2012 using a Gaussian approximation [eftekharzadeh2012noise]. The noise kernel is the symmetrized correlation of stress fluctuations about their mean [eftekharzadeh2012noise]. They treated nearby points separated by a timelike or spacelike interval, including fields in the Hartle-Hawking state [eftekharzadeh2012noise]. Charis Anastopoulos and Ntina Savvidou modeled a black hole and self gravitating radiation in a reflecting cavity in 2016 using the maximum entropy principle [anastopoulos2016equilibrium]. The proper width of a layer near the horizon scales as the geometric mean of the Schwarzschild radius and the Planck length within their thermodynamic model [anastopoulos2016equilibrium].¶The anti-de Sitter potential confines thermal radiation and keeps the conformal field metric perturbation bounded throughout the exterior [taylor2021backreaction]. Peter Taylor and Cormac Breen extended the calculation to Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter holes in 2021, using the Page approximation for massless conformal fields and a modified DeWitt-Schwinger approximation for massive fields [taylor2021backreaction]. They calculated the changes to the horizon, surface gravity, minimum temperature, and photon sphere [taylor2021backreaction]. Gamal Gergess Lamee Nashed, Alnadhief H. A. Alfedeel, and Tiberiu Harko modeled the stress of thermal radiation in a finite cavity in 2026 with a minimal analytic expression constrained by conservation and horizon regularity [nashed2026cavity]. The mass and redshift perturbations shift the horizon, Hawking temperature, and canonical stability threshold within that model [nashed2026cavity].

coordinates.name: Areal Radius

parameters.description: The renormalized black hole mass as a length, with horizon $r=2M$
The areal radius of the reflecting wall, $R=r_{\rm B}$
The value of $w$ at the wall
The dimensionless scalar field mass correction
The dimensionless scalar field redshift correction
The value of $\rho$ at the wall, $B=\rho(R)$

coordinates.convention: The coordinate $r$ is the areal radius and $t$ is the time matched to the Schwarzschild exterior at the reflecting wall. A dot in the geodesic equations denotes differentiation with respect to an affine parameter.

related.text: The vacuum geometry underlying the scalar field calculation, recovered as $\hbar$ tends to zero [hochberg1994potential].
A black hole in anti-de Sitter space, with thermal radiation confined by its gravitational potential and reflecting boundary conditions [taylor2021backreaction, hawking1983].
A black hole threaded by a cosmic string, whose thermal properties Erik A. Martinez and James W. York, Jr. studied with the Euclidean action [martinez1990].
